ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and the gray shading inside the circle is distributed outside the central white square. The figure also draws two squares of the same size, with sides parallel to the horizontal/vertical directions of the image; they are offset from each other, and their overlapping part is exactly the central unshaded white square. It can be seen that all four vertices of this central white square lie on the circumference. Reasoning: The shaded part is the area of the circle minus the area of the central unshaded square. The radius of the circle is 3 cm, so the area of the circle is π·3^2 = 9π. The central white square is inscribed in this circle, so its diagonal is equal to the diameter of the circle, namely 6 cm. Let the side length of the central square be s, then s√2 = 6, so s = 6/√2 = 3√2. The area of the central square is (3√2)^2 = 18. Therefore the total shaded area is 9π - 18 = 9(π - 2).

raw_record.question_text: Two quadrates with the same size cover a circle, the radius of which is $3 \mathrm{~cm}$. Find the total area (in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$) of the shaded figure.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as two congruent axis-aligned squares whose overlap is the central unshaded square. The shaded region is the part of the circle outside this central overlap. The four corners of the central unshaded square lie on the circle, so that square is inscribed in the circle. From the text, the circle radius is 3 cm, so its diameter is 6 cm. Use the inscribed-square fact that the square's diagonal equals the circle diameter: side = 6/sqrt(2) = 3sqrt(2), so the central square area is 18. Subtract from the circle area 9pi to get the shaded area 9pi - 18 = 9(pi - 2).

method.method_draft: Read the picture as showing the shaded region split into four congruent circular segments around the central unshaded square: top, bottom, left, and right. The central square has its vertices on the circle, so adjacent vertices subtend a 90-degree central angle. From the text, r = 3. For one shaded segment, compute the area as a quarter-circle sector minus the right isosceles triangle formed by two radii to adjacent square vertices: sector area = (1/4)pi(3^2), triangle area = (1/2)(3)(3). Multiply this segment area by 4 to obtain 4(9pi/4 - 9/2) = 9pi - 18 = 9(pi - 2).
